title: Why Airplane Mode Still Drains Your Battery Overnight
hook: You switch on airplane mode and the battery still drops by morning. The radio was never the whole story.
description: An inside-the-system explainer of why a phone on airplane mode still loses charge overnight.

scenes.vo: On the surface, airplane mode looks like the phone sleeps. Dark screen, no signal bars, done.
scenes.caption: On the surface, airplane mode looks like the phone finally sleeps.
scenes.whyArt: clean exterior view of a dark phone in airplane mode

scenes.vo: Lift the lid and the phone is still awake, indexing files and checking for updates.
scenes.caption: Lift the lid and the phone is still awake inside.
scenes.whyArt: exploded cutaway showing background tasks running

scenes.vo: The quiet drain is the operating system, not the radio. Apps scheduled to refresh wake the chip.
scenes.caption: The drain is the operating system, not the radio.
scenes.whyArt: one highlighted component: the scheduler waking the chip

scenes.vo: Every wake costs battery, but it buys a phone that feels instant. That is the price.
scenes.caption: Every wake costs battery, but buys a phone that feels instant.
scenes.whyArt: two-sided balance: readiness against battery life

scenes.vo: Airplane mode silences the radios, not the whole machine built to stay ready.
scenes.caption: It silences the radios, not the whole machine.
scenes.whyArt: system-wide view of what airplane mode does and does not touch
